articles.title: Republican Senate Nominee Who Backed Trump’s War Now Eating Her Words
articles.description: The Republican Senate nominee in Iowa is trying to criticize the Iran war’s effect on ordinary people—without mentioning President Trump or her own voting history. “Iowans are being squeezed and shouldn’t have to foot the bill at the pump or the checkout line for the war in Iran. We need to use every option at our disposal to provide some relief from high prices,” Representative Ashley Hinson posted on X Monday. Not surprisingly, Hinson’s solution doesn’t mention how Trump created the mess in the first place. Hinson also didn’t mention her own voting record: She has voted six times against House resolutions calling for Trump to end the war. Instead, she suggests “suspending the gas tax, pausing diesel exports, unleashing E-15 everywhere we can, reinstating the $1/gallon biodiesel tax credit, and creating a diesel relief program to help our farmers and truckers being crushed by the high costs.” “These actions to lower costs are needed ASAP, and the war needs to be brought to a successful and immediate end,” Hinson said, adding that Iowa’s highway trust fund needed be “replenished, so that Iowans don’t suffer from crumbling roads and bridges while relief comes our way now.” Fuel prices have skyrocketed in the last seven months, thanks to Iran’s control of the Strait of Hormuz, and, more recently, the takeover of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea by Houthi forces in Yemen. The average price of gasoline as of Monday was $4.4786 nationally and $4.3698 in Iowa, according to the American Automobile Association . Diesel fuel prices are even worse: $6.5107 nationally and $6.3157 in Iowa, a state with a large agricultural economy whose equipment depends on diesel. Hinson is polling neck and neck with her Democratic opponent, state Representative Josh Turek, and is clearly worried that failing to acknowledge the war’s impact could hurt her in November. Trump won the state by 13 points in 2024, but Republicans and the president are polling lower and lower each day with the ongoing war only getting worse .

articles.title: Can cloud seeding fight drought? Startup Rainmaker just raised $100 million to find out
articles.description: Rainmaker, the weather modification startup focused on generating rain and snow through cloud seeding, announced today that it has raised $100 million in Series B funding. Investors including NOA VC, Upfront Ventures, DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital, and Dream Ventures participated in the round. Rainmaker declined to share an updated valuation as part of the news. Prior to this round, the company had raised $50.3 million in venture backing. Founded in 2023 (and dubbed “ the hardest startup in America ” by Fast Company ), Rainmaker has developed a fleet of custom drones that can withstand harsh conditions in order to “seed” precipitation. During flights, the drones release silver iodide, an ice-attracting particle, into clouds with promising conditions. The silver iodide serves as a catalyst, helping turn the cloud’s water droplets or ice crystals into precipitation. In recent months, the company says, it has made significant progress toward demonstrating the effectiveness of its seeding programs. Rainmaker says that it has data tying its flights to 145 million incremental gallons of freshwater: Its drones fly in programmed patterns, allowing researchers to distinguish their precipitation from naturally occurring precipitation. In August, test flights in Alaska’s Kenai Peninsula yielded 19 million gallons of precipitation over the course of three hours. Founder and CEO Augustus Doricko views the Alaska testing as a breakthrough moment. “That [research campaign] represents a significant, precedent-changing shift in our capacity to produce fresh water at scale for the ecosystems, communities, and industries that need it across the Colorado River Basin, the Great Salt Lake, the rest of the dry and arid western United States, and world over,” he says. The new funding will support the expansion of Rainmaker’s research team, including radar meteorologists, machine learning specialists, and aerosol chemists. Rainmaker also plans to continue collaborating with outside research teams in order to validate its results. Interest in weather modification is on the rise as climate change introduces new risks and concerns, from drought to increasingly powerful storms. Recast Systems, a newly-launched competitor, is seeding clouds with an organic compound in Texas and New Mexico. Doricko says that Rainmaker has filed patents for multiple biodegradable seeding agents and is preparing to test them this winter. If Rainmaker continues to make progress toward cloud seeding at scale, Doricko sees an opportunity to mitigate extreme weather, too. Hail storms, floods, tornadoes, hurricanes: it’s not hard to imagine that someone will be willing to pay to make events such as these less severe. “We will be better situated than anybody in history to conduct these subsequent interventions,” Doricko says. They fit within his broader vision to “make Earth more habitable.”

articles.title: How one branding agency redesigned its website to reduce carbon emissions
articles.description: After one Australian branding agency discovered its website produced more carbon than the average webpage, it redesigned it to be more efficient. In the process, the agency learned something about striking the right balance between sustainability and style. MEK is a Melbourne studio that’s worked with clients like the conservation groups WWF Australia and Sea Shepherd . During a trivia night in 2022, its team learned that sending 100 emails has a bigger carbon footprint than driving one kilometer (five-eighths of a mile) in a car. That surprising statistic led the agency to audit its own website and learn that it produced more carbon than 76.5% of web pages tested on the online Website Carbon calculator . Websites can be made more sustainable by design , and there are even some digital fonts that use less energy than others . Digital technology is estimated to account for 3.7% of global greenhouse emissions, according to the Shift Project, a think tank. Reducing that through a more sustainably designed web is not just better for the planet, it’s a faster experience for the user too. To go about redesigning its website , completed in 2023 and updated this year, MEK first examined what was making it score so poorly on the carbon calculator. The agency’s homepage had a looped slideshow that included seven full-screen images and white backgrounds that looked clean but were more energy intensive than dark mode. It also found unnecessarily duplicated HTML tags that slowed the site down. There were several changes MEK could make to its site, but some came with aesthetic considerations—no small matter for any branding, creative, or design agency that uses its web page to showcase its taste and personality and wow and inspire potential clients. For MEK, striking the right balance between efficiency and design considerations was especially tricky when it came to font selection. Agency employees tried different fonts, shifting from the smart, confident sans serif Monument Grotesk to Arial , an overused sans serif disliked by designers and type snobs but widely available. Fonts like Arial that come in default mode on Macs, PCs, and smartphone operating systems use less energy because when you visit a web page that uses them, the browser doesn’t have to make additional requests to servers. The problem for a branding agency, though, is that it looks basic. “The most sustainable fonts are the system fonts already installed on devices because they don’t need to be downloaded, which uses less energy and therefore produces fewer emissions,” says Mirella Arapian, MEK’s founder and executive creative director, who led the project. “However, these fonts offer less typographic control and are generally less expressive. Making them work well involves a high level of experience, and even then, they may not deliver the character a brand needs to be distinctive.” MEK now uses Zalando Sans , a Google Font. Google Fonts are widely used and efficiently served and cached by web browsers. And many of them are created by reputable type foundries. The agency also cleaned up its duplicated HTML tags, set the page to dark mode with white text at 87% opacity, and improved the efficiency of its images. MEK’s carbon performance has improved, from producing more carbon than 76.5% of web pages tested back in 2022 to being cleaner than 74% of all web pages globally in 2026, according to a review on Website Carbon calculator. Arapian says MEK has incorporated its carbon-centered redesign learning into its work with clients, educating them about the environmental impact of their digital footprint and giving them the information they need to make informed choices. “When we first set out with this project we wanted carbon emissions to be as low as possible, but through the process we realized that the goal isn’t to eliminate everything just because it has an environmental cost, but to be honest about whether it earns its place in the overall experience,” she tells Fast Company . By making informed design choices, web designers can deliver an internet experience that’s more efficient and looks good too.

Moon alert

Avoid shopping (except food and gas) and important decisions from 9 a.m. to 12:45 p.m. Chicago time. After that, the moon moves from Capricorn into Aquarius.

A positive day

A positive day

Although this is a positive day with lots of upbeat energy to get things done, be aware that bosses, parents, VIPs and the police might throw you a curveball. They might say or do something you least expect. ("Busted!")

A dynamic day

Unexpected opportunities to travel, as well as explore avenues in publishing, the media, medicine, the law and higher education, could be a blessing today because you're full of creative ideas! The arts, sports and activities with children hold promising adventures.

A positive day

Be ready to compromise today because this might be a factor you have to deal with. Double-check banking details and anything to do with shared property and inheritances because something might surprise you. Fortunately, family discussions are positive and encouraging!

Leo (July 23-Aug. 22)

A positive day

Your communication skills are excellent today because you're a walking example of the power of positive thinking. Don't hesitate to entertain big plans that might include shopping for beautiful things for your home and entertaining. Meanwhile, a spouse, partner or close friend may surprise you.

Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22)

A dynamic day

Ka-ching! This is an excellent day for financial negotiations. Trust your moneymaking ideas. However, if shopping, you might be tempted to spend big. (Keep your receipts.) Meanwhile, something to do with your job, your health or your pet might surprise you. Stay tuned.

Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22)

A dynamic day

Today Mercury is in your sign dancing with lucky Jupiter, which makes you feel happy and friendly. Group activities will appeal. You might be concerned for the welfare of others. Parents should be vigilant because this is a mildly accident-prone day for your kids. Expect social plans to change.

Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21)

A positive day

You might be caught off guard by a family discussion or a family member, probably a female, who has strong feelings about something. Tread carefully. Meanwhile, hidden news might be revealed that pleases you. You might see ways to shine your reputation in the eyes of others.

Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21)

A positive day

Pay attention to everything you say and do today because this is a mildly accident-prone day. Nevertheless, your dealings with friends, groups and organizations will be positive and successful because young people will respond to your inspirational ideas. (You’re impressive.)

Capricorn (Dec. 22-Jan. 19)

A positive day

Keep an eye on your money and possessions today because something unexpected could impact them. Guard against loss, theft or damage. Meanwhile, you will impress bosses, parents and VIPs with your visionary ideas. Your mind is clear, sharp and quick to see the big picture.

Aquarius (Jan. 20-Feb. 18)

A dynamic day

Today your feelings are intense. Your routine might be interrupted by something unexpected. But you might be encouraged by something related to politics, the news, medicine, the law or higher education. Or perhaps you have a chance to travel. Something definitely lifts your spirits!

Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20)

A positive day

This is an excellent day for financial discussions, especially regarding shared property, inheritances, taxes, debt and insurance issues because whatever happens, you'll come out smelling like a rose. Work-related travel is likely for some of you. Whatever happens will probably improve your job or your chances to get a better job.

This is a year about creating solid foundations in your life, both physically and internally. Simplicity is key. Take charge of your health. Exercise will play an important role. articles.title: Starwatch: Autumnal equinox in northern hemisphere, spring in the south
articles.description: Precise moment of equinox in UK is 1.05am on Wednesday – but day and night will not be equal until Friday The September or autumnal equinox takes place this week. It marks the astronomical beginning of autumn in the northern hemisphere and spring in the southern hemisphere. This year, the precise moment of the equinox falls at 01.05 BST on 23 September. It is commonly said the equinox is when day and night are equal, because the name derives from the Latin for “equal night”, but in practice that is not quite true. An equinox occurs when the sun crosses the celestial equator, the imaginary projection of Earth’s equator into the sky. Continue reading...
